cues.text: Hello, Jane Fairbanks speaking.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Oh, good morning. My name's Frank Pritchard.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: I've just retired and moved to Southoe.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: I'd like to become a volunteer, and I gather you co-ordinate voluntary work in the village.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: That's right.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: What sort of thing could I do?
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Well, we need help with the village library.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: We borrow books from the town library, and individuals also donate them.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: So, one thing you could do is get involved in collecting them - if you've got a car, that is.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Yes, that's no problem.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: The times are pretty flexible so we can arrange it to suit you.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Another thing is the records that we keep of the books we're given, and those we borrow and need to return to the town library.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: It would be very useful to have another person to help keep them up to date.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Right. I'm used to working on a computer - presume they're computerised?
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Oh yes.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Is the library purpose-built?
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: I haven't noticed it when I've walked round the village.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: No, we simply have the use of a room in the village hall, the West Room.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: It's on the left as you go in.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: I must go and have a look inside the hall.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Yes, it's a nice building.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Do you run a lunch club in the village for elderly people?
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: I know a lot of places do.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Yes, we have a very successful club.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: I could help with transport, if that's of any use.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Ooo definitely. People come to the club from neighbouring villages, and we're always in need of more drivers.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: And does the club have groups that focus on a particular hobby, too?
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: I could get involved in one or two, particularly if there are any art groups.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Excellent. I'll find out where we need help and get back to you.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Fine. What about help for individual residents.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Do you arrange that at all?
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Yes, we do it as a one-off.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: In fact, there's Mrs Carroll.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: She needs a lift to the hospital next week, and we're struggling to find someone.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: When's her appointment?
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: On Tuesday. It would take the whole morning.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: I could do that.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Oh, that would be great.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Thank you. And also, next week, we're arranging to have some work done to Mr Selsbury's house before he moves, as he isn't healthy enough to do it himself.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: We've got some people to decorate his kitchen, but if you could do some weeding in his garden, that would be wonderful.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: OK. I'd enjoy that.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: And presumably the day and time are flexible.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Oh yes. Just say when would suit you best, and we'll let Mr Selsbury know.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Good.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: The volunteers group also organises monthly social events, which is a great way to meet other people, of course.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Uhuh.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: So next month, on the 19th of October, we're holding a quiz - a couple of residents are great at planning unusual ones, and we always fill the village hall.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: That sounds like fun. Can I do anything to help?
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Well, because of the number of people, we need plenty of refreshments for halfway through.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: So, if you could provide any, we'd be grateful.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: I'm sure I could.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: I'll think about what to make, and let you know.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Thank you. Then on November the 18th, we're holding a dance, also in the village hall.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: We've booked a band that specialises in music of the 1930s - they've been before, and we've had a lot of requests to bring them back.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: I'm not really a dancer, but I'd like to do something to help.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Well, we sell tickets in advance, and having an extra person to check them at the door, as people arrive, would be good - it can be quite a bottleneck if everyone arrives at once!
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: OK, I'm happy with that.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: We're also arranging a New Year's Eve party.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: We're expecting that to be a really big event, so instead of the village hall, it'll be held in the Mountfort Hotel.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: The ...?
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Mountfort. M-O-U-N-T-F-O-R-T Hotel. It isn't in Southoe itself, but it's only a couple of miles away.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: The hotel will be providing dinner and we've booked a band.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: The one thing we haven't got yet is a poster.
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: That isn't something you could do, by any chance, is it?
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Well actually, yes.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Before I retired I was a graphic designer, so that's right up my street.
cues.speaker: FRANK

cues.text: Oh perfect! I'll give you the details, and then perhaps you could send me a draft …
cues.speaker: JANE

cues.text: Of course.
cues.speaker: FRANK
